summary.intent: Reduce git process scaling in a large monorepo tool, specifically making `version --emit-preview` stop running one `git diff` per changed package, and ship it as a reviewed PR alongside several other open PRs.
summary.outcome: Opened PR #494, which runs one diff per distinct last-tag commit (150 changed packages: 151 diffs and 3.8 s down to 4 diffs and 1.0 s). It has a PR body, a patch changeset, and a link to trail 250. Re-ran the flaky macos-arm64 job on #490 and #487 and both passed. CI for #491, #492 and #494 has not been checked.

repo: AGENTS.md forbids spawning a git process per package; `changed_source_files_since_last_tag` violated it by running one `git diff` per package.

The batched diff attributes each path to every package whose directory contains it, so an outer package still owns an inner package's files; narrowing this could drop an outer package from release proposals.
Untagged or directory-less packages still need one git call each.
Pathspecs are split across several diffs past 24,000 bytes to stay under the Windows 32 KB command-line limit.
Pre-merge checks are `just pre-push`, `just lint`, `just doc-check`, `just test` and `just workflow-contracts`; they need to run outside the sandbox.
Before the change, `status`, `version --dry-run` and the publish plan were flat in package count (8 to 23 git processes, under 2.6 s at 1,800 packages on a debug build).
workflow: Measuring with a synthetic monorepo (up to 1,500 Cargo crates plus 300 npm packages) and counting git processes gave concrete before/after numbers.
A differential test against a per-package reference, plus mutation checks (removing batching or the budget must fail tests), validates a batching refactor.
A one-byte budget test forces chunking and shows the split changes no results.
Sandbox network restrictions cause false test failures; rerun outside the sandbox.
A macos-arm64 CI failure was runner capacity, not code; re-running the job fixed it.
A background agent can draft the PR body while the main session continues; the main session applies it with `gh pr edit --body-file`.

friction: The implementer's three 'network' test failures were sandbox artifacts.
macos-arm64 CI failures on #490 and #487 came from runner capacity and needed a re-run.
The brief's spec on nested packages conflicted with the implementer's behavior and needed a judgment call.
A merge conflict on the user's PR #492 had to be resolved and pushed.
